verses.zh: 你们要赞美耶和华！耶和华的仆人哪，你们要赞美，赞美耶和华的名！
verses.en: Praise the Lord.Praise, you servants of the Lord,praise the name of the Lord.

verses.zh: 耶和华的名是应当称颂的，从今时直到永远！
verses.en: May the Lord’s name be praisednow and forevermore.

verses.zh: 从日出之地到日落之处，耶和华的名是应当赞美的！
verses.en: From east to west[NOTE:1] the Lord’s name is deserving of praise.
notes: Psalm 113. The psalmist praises God as the sovereign king of the world who reaches down to help the needy.

verses.zh: 耶和华超乎万民之上；他的荣耀高过诸天。
verses.en: The Lord is exalted over all the nations;his splendor reaches beyond the sky.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “from the rising of the sun to its setting.” The extent is not temporal (“from sunrise to sunset”) but spatial (“from the place where the sun rises [the east] to the place where it sets [the west].” In the phenomenological language of OT cosmology, the sun was described as rising in the east and setting in the west.

verses.zh: 谁像耶和华―我们的　神呢？他坐在至高之处，
verses.en: Who can compare to the Lord our God,who sits on a high throne?[NOTE:1]

verses.zh: 自己谦卑，观看天上地下的事。
verses.en: He bends down to look[NOTE:1] at the sky and the earth.
notes: Heb “the one who makes high to sit.”

verses.zh: 他从灰尘里抬举贫寒人，从粪堆中提拔穷乏人，
verses.en: He raises the poor from the dirtand lifts up the needy from the garbage pile[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “the one who makes low to see.”

verses.zh: 使他们与王子同坐，就是与本国的王子同坐。
verses.en: that he might seat him with princes,with the princes of his people.

verses.zh: 他使不能生育的妇人安居家中，为多子的乐母。你们要赞美耶和华！
verses.en: He makes the barren woman of the family[NOTE:1] a happy mother of children.[NOTE:2] Praise the Lord.
notes: The language of v. 7 is almost identical to that of 1 Sam 2:8.

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which
means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the
light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not
relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare
your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is
the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every
paragraph has one and only one subject.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 113:1-4

1Praise the Lord!

Praise, O servants of the Lord,

Praise the name of the Lord.

2Blessed be the name
of the Lord

From this time forth and
forever.

3From the rising of
the sun to its setting

The name of the
Lord is to be praised.

4The
Lord is high above all nations;

His glory is above the
heavens.

113:1 This verse has the same IMPERATIVE repeated three times for emphasis (BDB 237, KB 248,
Piel IMPERATIVE; see same technique in Ps. 96:1-2). It starts out like Psalms 111; 112 (see note at
Ps. 111:1). This Psalm reveals why YHWH should be praised.

- He is above all nations, Ps. 113:4

- His glory is above the heavens, Ps. 113:4

- he is unique (see SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM),
Ps. 113:5

- He humbles Himself to know and be involved in the lives of His faithful followers, Ps. 113:6 (cf. Ps. 18:35c)

- He cares for those who are socially ostracized and who have no power, Ps. 113:7-9 (cf. Ps. 109:31)

- the poor

- the needy

- the barren

▣ "the Lord" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

▣ "O servants of the Lord" The AB (p. 131) changes the vowels and
makes this "the works of the Lord." This form (BDB 714) is found in Eccl. 9:1.

If the MT is correct, "servants" would refer to

- angels (cf. Ps. 103:20-22; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: HEAVENLY COUNCIL OF ANGELS)

- worshipers in the temple (cf. Deut. 32:43; Ps. 34:22; 69:36; 105:25; 135:14)

- Levites/priests in the temple (cf. Ps. 134:1; 135:1-2)

▣ "the name of the Lord See
SPECIAL TOPIC: "THE NAME" OF YHWH.

113:2 "Blessed be the name of the Lord" This VERB
(BDB 138, KB 159, Pual PARTICIPLE combined with the JUSSIVE
form of the VERB "to be") is parallel to "praise" (cf. Ps. 145:21).

SPECIAL TOPIC: "THE NAME" OF YHWH

113:2b-3a These two lines are parallel and in figurative language to express the extent of the praise of YHWH

- for all time, Ps. 113:2b (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: FOREVER ['olam])

- in all places, Ps. 113:3a

113:4 "high above all nations" This verse tells why He should be praised.

- He is high above all nations (cf. Ps. 97:9; 99:2)

- His glory is above the heavens (cf. Ps. 8:1; 57:11; 148:13)

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEAVEN

▣ "glory" See SPECIAL TOPIC: GLORY (DOXA).

113:5 "Who is like the Lord our God" Notice both YHWH and Elohim are
used for the Deity of Israel.

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, C., D.

▣ "Who is enthroned on high" This is parallel to Ps. 113:4b. It is an idiom of kingship (cf. Ps. 103:19). YHWH
is king (note 1 Sam. 8:7). The ancient Israelites viewed their God as sitting on His throne above the atmosphere of the
earth with His feet resting (i.e., footstool) on the ark of the covenant. The ark's lid was where heaven and earth symbolically met!

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEAVEN AND THE THIRD HEAVEN

113:6

NASB, NKJV
"Who humbles Himself"

NRSV
"who looks far down"

TEV, NET
"he bends down to see"

NJB
"he stoops to look down"

JPSOA
"see what is below"

REB
"deigns to look down so low"

LXX
"looks upon that which is lowly"

This unusual phrase denotes that YHWH knows what is happening on earth, especially to
His people (cf. Exod. 3:7-8; Ps. 138:6a,b).

The LXX translates this verse as YHWH looking on the "lowly" (i.e., humans).

The Peshitta translates it as "the deep" and makes it one of three levels of this planet.

- atmosphere

- land

- water (the deep)

▣ "in heaven and in the earth" This is speaking of this planet and its atmosphere.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEAVEN

113:9a,b All of the wives of the early Patriarchs were barren, but YHWH opened their wombs.

- Sarah ‒ Gen. 21:6

- Rebekah ‒ Gen. 25:21

- Rachel ‒ Gen. 30:22-23

However, a child was a special act of YHWH to show

- His care

- His power

- His plan for Israel and the whole world (cf. Ps. 113:4)

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

113:9c The Psalm ends as it began. Some scholars see this line as the beginning of the next Psalm (LXX). This
phrase is the introduction to Psalms 111; 112; 113.
